title: Preserve versions and recover an earlier one
goal: Recover v1 without losing v2 or the current source.
challenge: Retain both backups and recover alpha from the earlier version into a separate directory while current source says alpha-v2. Detect a wrong-version restore using expected contents, not a successful tar listing.

steps.command: w=/home/learner/ll-backup-7; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
steps.explanation: Guard a fresh, learner-owned workspace and check guest free space. Stop if any command fails.
steps.expected: Private practice directory; at least 65536 KiB available.

steps.command: guard() { test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-backup-7 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-backup-7 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && test -z "$(find . -type l -print -quit)"; }; guard
steps.explanation: Define and use a location/owner guard for every later change.
steps.expected: Exact physical path, not a link.

steps.command: guard && mkdir -m 0700 source && printf 'alpha\n' > source/note.txt && printf 'bravo\n' > 'source/space name.txt' && chmod 0640 source/note.txt && chmod 0600 'source/space name.txt' && touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC' source/note.txt 'source/space name.txt'
steps.explanation: Create two known regular files, including a name with a space.
steps.expected: alpha and bravo lines, modes640/600, fixed UTC timestamp.

steps.command: guard && test ! -e v1.tar && test ! -L v1.tar && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -cf v1.tar -C source -- note.txt 'space name.txt' && test "$(stat -c %s v1.tar)" -le 65536

guard && test ! -e v2.tar && test ! -L v2.tar && test ! -e versions.sha256 && test ! -L versions.sha256 && printf 'alpha-v2\n' > source/note.txt && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -cf v2.tar -C source -- note.txt 'space name.txt' && sha256sum -- v1.tar v2.tar > versions.sha256
steps.explanation: Distinct names; never overwrite a previous backup. Refuse existing backup/reference names before changing source or writing an archive.
steps.expected: Two differing snapshots, current source v2.

steps.command: guard && mkdir -m 0700 wrong restore && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -xf v2.tar -C wrong --no-same-owner --same-permissions && printf 'alpha\n' | cmp - wrong/note.txt; printf 'wrong version status=%s\n' "$?"
steps.explanation: Wrong backup is structurally fine but not the required version.

steps.command: guard && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -xf v1.tar -C restore --no-same-owner --same-permissions && printf 'alpha\n' | cmp - restore/note.txt && printf 'alpha-v2\n' | cmp - source/note.txt && sha256sum -c -- versions.sha256
steps.explanation: Recover v1, retain live v2 and both unchanged backups.
steps.expected: All checks pass; originals/prior backups preserved.

hints: A valid archive can be the wrong recovery point.
Keep both snapshots and compare the requested version.
review: Wrong-version mismatch, restoredalpha, currentalpha-v2, unchanged v1/v2digests.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 103.3 and LPIC-2 v4.5 206.2 partial manual archives/recovery; 104.5 reinforcement where applicable. Self-reviewed, unscored; not complete objectives.
